about: Ready-made four-person poster recipes written by Claude. Copy a film's menu straight into its edition block. Do not edit this file.

s.note: Warm blini with crème fraîche, smoked salmon, salmon roe and dill.
s.how: Warm 16 cocktail blini on a tray at 180C for 4 minutes. Top each with 1 tsp crème fraîche, a curl of smoked salmon (about 150g in total), 1/2 tsp salmon roe and a small sprig of dill. Pass around on a tray straight away so the blini are still warm.

s.note: Cashews and almonds roasted with butter, rosemary, brown sugar and cayenne.
s.how: Melt 30g butter with 1 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tsp chopped rosemary, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper and 1/2 tsp salt. Toss through 150g cashews and 150g almonds, spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes, stirring halfway. Cool for 5 minutes so they crisp, then serve warm in a glass bowl.

m.note: Shaved rare roast beef in soft rolls with horseradish cream and rocket.
m.how: Rub a 1kg beef topside with 1 tbsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp cracked pepper and 1 tsp salt. Roast at 200C for about 35 minutes until 52C inside, then rest 15 minutes and shave thin. Stir 2 tbsp horseradish into 150ml sour cream. Split 8 soft rolls, spread with the horseradish cream and fill with beef, 60g rocket and 100g pickled onions, sliced.

w.note: Vanilla sponge fingers split and piped with fluffy marshmallow cream.
w.how: Beat 125g soft butter with 150g caster sugar, add 3 eggs one at a time and 1 tsp vanilla extract, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 80ml milk. Bake in a lined 20 by 30cm tin at 180C for 22 minutes, cool and cut into 12 fingers. For the cream, boil 150g caster sugar with 50ml water to 118C and pour into 2 egg whites whisking hard until thick and glossy. Split the fingers and pipe the cream inside.

d.note: Bourbon over one big ice cube with a strip of orange peel.
d.how: Put one large ice cube in each of four heavy tumblers. Pour 45ml bourbon over each, about 180ml in total. Peel 4 wide strips of orange zest, twist each over a glass to release the oil and drop it in. Serve straight away.

s.note: Golden chickpea fritters fried crisp, finished with lemon and salt.
s.how: Whisk 250g chickpea flour into 750ml cold water with 1 tsp salt until smooth. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 10 minutes until very thick. Add 2 tbsp chopped parsley, spread 1cm thick on an oiled tray and leave to set for 1 hour. Cut into squares and fry in 180C oil until puffed and golden. Drain, salt, and serve with lemon wedges.

s.note: Ripe rockmelon wedges draped with prosciutto, pepper and olive oil.
s.how: Leave 1 rockmelon at room temperature for an hour. Halve, scoop out the seeds, cut into 12 long wedges and cut off the skin. Drape each wedge with a slice of prosciutto (about 150g in total), add a crack of black pepper and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil just before serving.

m.note: Rigatoni with fried eggplant, tomato and basil, under grated ricotta salata.
m.how: Cut 2 eggplants into thick half moons and fry in batches in 120ml olive oil until deep gold, drain. Fry 3 sliced garlic cloves in 2 tbsp of the oil, add 800g San Marzano tomatoes and a handful of basil, simmer 20 minutes and season. Cook 500g rigatoni until al dente, toss with the sauce, eggplant and a splash of pasta water. Grate 100g ricotta salata heavily over the top.

w.note: Crisp shells filled with sweet ricotta, candied orange and pistachio.
w.how: Drain 500g fresh ricotta in a sieve for 2 hours. Beat with 80g icing sugar, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon and 40g finely chopped candied orange peel. Spoon into a piping bag and fill 8 cannoli shells just before serving. Dip each end in 30g chopped pistachios and dust with a little more icing sugar.

d.note: Sicilian red opened early and served at cellar temperature.
d.how: Open one 750ml bottle of Nero d'Avola 30 minutes before dinner and keep it at about 16C, cooler than the room. Pour into four large glasses, about 180ml each, with no ice.

s.note: Buttery potato and slow-cooked onion baked in golden puff pastry.
s.how: Boil 500g peeled potatoes 15 minutes, drain and mash. Cook 1 finely diced brown onion in 30g butter over low heat for 15 minutes until golden, then mix into the mash with salt and white pepper. Cut 2 sheets puff pastry into 4 squares each, fill, fold into parcels and brush with 1 beaten egg. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with 40g hot English mustard.

s.note: Thin baked bagel crisps with chive cream cheese and smoked salmon.
s.how: Slice 3 day-old bagels into thin rounds, brush with 2 tbsp olive oil and bake at 180C for 12 minutes until crisp. Beat 250g cream cheese with 2 tbsp chopped chives and the zest of 1 lemon. Serve the crisps with the schmear and 150g smoked salmon on the side.

m.note: Slow-braised brisket on sweet onions, sliced thick with rich gravy.
m.how: Season a 1.5kg beef brisket with salt and pepper and sear hard on all sides. Slice 3 brown onions into a roasting dish, sit the brisket on top, and pour over 500ml beef stock whisked with 2 tbsp tomato paste and 2 tsp sweet paprika. Cover and braise at 150C for 4 hours. Rest 20 minutes, slice against the grain, and boil the juices for 10 minutes to make gravy.

w.note: Sponge cups piped high with vanilla cream and a cherry.
w.how: Cut 8 rounds from a 300g sponge cake to fit the bottom of 8 paper cups. Whip 300ml thickened cream with 100g mascarpone, 2 tbsp icing sugar and 1 tsp vanilla extract to firm peaks. Pipe high over the sponge in a tall swirl and top each with a maraschino cherry. Chill 30 minutes before serving.

d.note: Rye whiskey poured neat into china coffee cups.
d.how: Pour 45ml rye whiskey, about 180ml in total, into each of four china coffee cups, the way it was served when it was illegal. Put a small jug of cold water on the table so everyone can add a splash.

s.note: Grilled ciabatta with tomato and garlic sliced as thin as possible.
s.how: Slice 6 garlic cloves paper thin on a mandoline and cook in 80ml extra virgin olive oil over low heat for 5 minutes until soft and barely golden. Grill 8 slices of ciabatta, rub with the cut side of 2 halved tomatoes and season with salt. Spoon the garlic and its oil over the top and finish with torn basil.

s.note: Poached prawns on crisp iceberg with a brandy Marie Rose sauce.
s.how: Poach 500g peeled green prawns for 2 minutes in salted water with a slice of lemon, then chill in iced water. Mix 120g mayonnaise with 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce, a few drops of hot sauce and 1 tsp brandy. Shred half an iceberg lettuce into four coupes, add the prawns and spoon over the sauce. Dust with paprika and serve with lemon wedges.

m.note: Veal, beef and pork meatballs simmered in a thin-garlic tomato sauce.
m.how: Soak 2 slices bread in 80ml milk, then mix with 200g veal mince, 200g beef mince, 200g pork mince, 1 egg, 40g grated pecorino, chopped parsley and 1 crushed garlic clove. Roll into 16 balls and brown. In the same pot gently cook 4 garlic cloves sliced razor thin and half a diced onion, add 800g San Marzano tomatoes and the meatballs and simmer 90 minutes. Serve over 500g spaghetti.

w.note: Fluffy scraped lemon ice served in little paper cups.
w.how: Simmer 200g caster sugar with 500ml water and the zest of 2 lemons for 5 minutes, then cool. Stir in 250ml lemon juice, about 6 lemons. Pour into a shallow tray and freeze, scraping with a fork every 30 minutes for 3 hours until light and fluffy. Serve in paper cups.

d.note: Blended Scotch over ice in a tall glass, topped with soda.
d.how: Fill four highball glasses with ice. Pour 45ml blended Scotch into each, about 180ml in total, and top with chilled soda water, about 120ml each. No garnish, the way it was poured at the Bamboo Lounge.

s.note: Saffron rice balls filled with beef ragù, peas and mozzarella.
s.how: Cook 300g arborio rice in 900ml stock with a pinch of saffron until thick, stir in 40g parmesan and chill overnight on a tray. Brown 150g beef mince with 50g frozen peas and 2 tbsp passata. Wrap golf balls of rice around a spoon of filling and a cube of mozzarella. Roll in flour, 2 beaten eggs and 100g breadcrumbs, and fry at 175C until deep gold.

s.note: Pressed slider rolls of ham, mojo pork, Swiss cheese and pickle.
s.how: Split 8 slider rolls and smear the cut sides with 2 tbsp yellow mustard. Layer with 150g leg ham, 150g sliced roast pork, 8 slices Swiss cheese and sliced dill pickles. Brush the tops with 30g melted butter and press in a heavy pan over medium heat with a second pan on top, 3 minutes a side, until the cheese melts.

m.note: Baked ziti with sausage tomato sauce, seasoned ricotta and blistered mozzarella.
m.how: Squeeze 500g Italian sausages from their skins and brown, add 700ml passata and simmer 30 minutes. Cook 500g ziti or penne 3 minutes short of done. Mix 400g ricotta with 50g grated parmesan, nutmeg and parsley. Layer pasta, sauce and ricotta in a baking dish, top with 200g torn mozzarella and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until blistered.

w.note: Vanilla slab cake iced pale green and cut like an island.
w.how: Beat 200g soft butter with 200g caster sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour with 100ml milk. Bake in a lined slab tin at 180C for 30 minutes and cool. Trim into a rough island shape. Beat 150g butter with 300g icing sugar and a few drops of green food colouring, spread thinly then again, pipe happy birthday across and slice at the table.

d.note: White rum, fresh lime and sugar shaken hard and served ice cold.
d.how: Make sugar syrup by dissolving 60g caster sugar in 60ml hot water and cooling. For each drink shake 60ml white rum, 25ml fresh lime juice and 15ml syrup hard with plenty of ice, then double strain into a chilled coupe. Makes four, with 240ml rum and about 4 limes.

s.note: Flaky pastry cases with a silky just-set egg custard.
s.how: Dissolve 70g caster sugar in 120ml hot water and cool. Whisk in 3 eggs, 80ml evaporated milk and 40ml full cream milk, then strain. Cut 12 rounds from 2 sheets puff pastry and press into a greased patty tin. Fill three quarters full and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until the custard is just set with a slight wobble.

s.note: Crisp salt and pepper prawns tossed with fried garlic and chilli.
s.how: Dry 500g shell-on green prawns well, season with salt and white pepper and toss in 60g potato starch. Fry in batches at 190C for 2 minutes until crisp. In a wok, fry 4 sliced garlic cloves, 1 sliced red chilli and 2 sliced spring onions in a little oil for 30 seconds, add the prawns and toss well.

m.note: Five spice roast duck with lacquered skin, plum sauce and rice.
m.how: Rub the cavity of a 2kg whole duck with 2 tsp five spice and 1 tsp salt, and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight to dry the skin. Brush with 2 tbsp honey loosened with hot water and roast at 180C for 90 minutes, brushing again twice. Rest 15 minutes and chop through the bone. Serve with 150ml plum sauce and 2 cups jasmine rice.

w.note: Chilled mango and coconut cream with sago pearls and pomelo.
w.how: Boil 80g sago pearls in plenty of water for 15 minutes until clear, then rinse under cold water and chill. Blend the flesh of 2 mangoes with 200ml coconut milk and 100ml evaporated milk. Fold in the sago, divide into bowls and top with diced mango from a third mango and segments of half a pomelo.

d.note: Strong black tea strained smooth with evaporated milk and sugar.
d.how: Simmer 4 tbsp loose black tea in 800ml water for 5 minutes. Strain twice through a fine cloth or sieve for a smooth tea. Add 200ml evaporated milk and 4 tsp caster sugar, stir, and serve hot or poured over ice.

s.note: Lacy salt cod fritters with garlic and coriander.
s.how: Soak 250g salt cod for 24 hours, changing the water three times, then flake. Whisk 200g plain flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 300ml water, 2 crushed garlic cloves and a handful of chopped coriander into a loose batter and fold in the cod. Fry wide flat spoonfuls in 180C oil until golden and lacy, drain and salt.

s.note: Twice-fried smashed green plantain with garlic and lime mojo.
s.how: Peel 3 green plantains and cut into 3cm chunks. Fry at 160C for 4 minutes until soft, smash flat with a heavy glass and fry again at 190C until crisp. Salt well. Mix 3 crushed garlic cloves with the juice of 2 limes and 60ml olive oil and spoon over.

m.note: Garlic and oregano roast pork shoulder with crackling, rice and pigeon peas.
m.how: Stab a 2kg pork shoulder all over and rub with 8 crushed garlic cloves, 2 tsp dried oregano, 2 tsp salt and 2 tbsp white vinegar. Marinate overnight. Roast skin up at 160C for 5 hours, then 230C for 20 minutes to crackle. Cook 400g long grain rice with a 400g tin of pigeon peas, stock and a little onion to serve alongside.

w.note: Coconut caramel flan, baked slowly and turned out cold.
w.how: Melt 150g caster sugar in a pan until deep amber and pour into a ring tin. Blend a 395g tin condensed milk, 270ml coconut milk, 375ml evaporated milk and 5 eggs and pour over the caramel. Bake in a water bath at 160C for 50 minutes until just set. Chill overnight, run a knife around and turn out onto a plate.

d.note: Golden rum over ice with cold cola and a big squeeze of lime.
d.how: Fill four tall glasses with ice. Pour 45ml golden rum into each, about 180ml in total, top with cold cola and squeeze in a big wedge of lime, about 2 limes for four drinks.

s.note: Clams under golden garlic, oregano and parmesan crumbs.
s.how: Steam 1kg clams with a splash of water in a covered pan until they open, about 4 minutes, and discard any closed ones. Remove the top shells. Mix 60g breadcrumbs, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tsp dried oregano, 30g grated parmesan and 3 tbsp olive oil. Top each clam and grill for 3 minutes until golden.

s.note: Prosciutto on rockmelon, with bocconcini dressed in bright basil oil.
s.how: Cut 1 rockmelon into 12 skinless wedges and drape with 120g prosciutto. Blitz a bunch of basil with 80ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Drain 220g bocconcini, dress with the basil oil and cracked pepper and serve beside the melon.

m.note: Seared veal escalopes in a glossy mushroom and marsala sauce.
m.how: Dust 600g veal escalopes in seasoned flour and sear in butter and oil for 1 minute a side, then set aside. Brown 250g sliced button mushrooms in the same pan, add 150ml marsala and 150ml beef stock and reduce by half. Whisk in 40g cold butter, return the veal and warm through for a minute. Serve with crusty bread.

w.note: Warm whisked marsala custard spooned over fresh strawberries.
w.how: Whisk 4 egg yolks, 60g caster sugar and 80ml marsala in a heatproof bowl over simmering water for 6 to 8 minutes until thick, pale and tripled in volume. Spoon warm over 250g halved strawberries in four glasses and serve straight away.

d.note: Chianti Classico decanted and poured with a flourish.
d.how: Decant one 750ml bottle of Chianti Classico 30 minutes before dinner and keep it at about 16C. Pour into four glasses, about 180ml each, the way Charlie would at the restaurant.

s.note: Blistered Italian sausage with charred onion and capsicum on toothpicks.
s.how: Grill 500g Italian sausages over high heat for 12 minutes, turning, until blistered and cooked through. Grill 1 red capsicum and 1 onion cut into chunks until charred at the edges. Slice the sausages thick and thread onto toothpicks with the capsicum and onion. Serve with 50g hot mustard.

s.note: Tender squid rings in a crisp semolina coat with lemon.
s.how: Slice 500g squid tubes into rings and soak in 250ml buttermilk for 30 minutes. Mix 100g fine semolina with 100g plain flour and plenty of salt. Drain the squid, toss in the flour mix and fry in 190C oil in batches for 90 seconds until pale gold. Salt and serve with 2 lemons cut into wedges.

m.note: Penne in a fiery garlic, chilli and tomato sauce with pecorino.
m.how: Gently fry 4 sliced garlic cloves and 1 tsp dried chilli flakes in 4 tbsp olive oil for 2 minutes. Add 800g crushed tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes, seasoning well. Cook 500g penne until al dente and toss through the sauce with a splash of pasta water and chopped parsley. Finish with 50g grated pecorino.

w.note: Hot fried dough puffs shaken in a bag of icing sugar.
w.how: Mix 250g plain flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tbsp caster sugar, a pinch of salt and 200ml warm water into a sticky batter and leave to rise for 1 hour. Drop teaspoons into 175C oil and fry 3 minutes until puffed and golden. Drain, tip into a paper bag with 60g icing sugar, shake and eat hot.

d.note: Cheap and cheerful Italian red in a jug, slightly chilled.
d.how: Chill one 750ml bottle of Italian red in the fridge for 20 minutes so it is just cool. Pour into a jug and serve in short tumblers, about 180ml each.

s.note: Chilled prawns on iceberg with horseradish Marie Rose.
s.how: Poach 500g peeled green prawns in salted water with lemon and a bay leaf for 2 minutes, then chill in iced water. Mix 120g mayonnaise with 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp horseradish and a squeeze of lemon. Shred half an iceberg lettuce into four glasses, hang the prawns off the rims and spoon the sauce into the middle.

s.n: Card table chips and onion dip
s.note: Thick-cut chips with a deep caramelised onion and chive dip.
s.how: Cook 2 thinly sliced brown onions in 2 tbsp oil over low heat for 40 minutes until deep brown, then cool. Mix with 200g sour cream, 100g cream cheese, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 2 tbsp chopped chives and salt. Serve with two 175g bags of thick-cut potato chips.

m.note: Butter-basted rib eye with thyme and garlic, and creamed spinach.
m.how: Salt 2 rib eye steaks, about 400g each, and leave uncovered on a rack in the fridge overnight. Sear in a smoking pan for 3 minutes a side, then add 50g butter, 4 sprigs thyme and 3 crushed garlic cloves and baste until 54C inside. Rest 8 minutes and slice. Wilt 500g spinach, squeeze dry and simmer with 150ml thickened cream and nutmeg.

w.note: Buttermilk muffins with exactly ten blueberries pressed into each.
w.how: Whisk 300g plain flour, 150g caster sugar and 2 tsp baking powder. Mix 2 eggs, 250ml buttermilk and 90g melted butter, then fold into the dry mix until just combined. Spoon into 12 lined muffin cases and press exactly 10 blueberries into the top of each. Bake at 190C for 20 minutes.

d.note: Gin stirred with a little vermouth, served in a frozen glass.
d.how: Freeze four martini glasses for 30 minutes. For each drink stir 60ml gin with 10ml dry vermouth over plenty of ice for 30 seconds and strain into a frozen glass. Garnish with a green olive on a pick. Makes four with 240ml gin and 40ml vermouth.
